subject: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@cloudscale.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>, Jamie Liao <jamie.l@cloudscale.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:33 -0500
Subject: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence

Rafael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement and engineering reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and we have a couple of asks before we can move to legal review:

- Target uptime uplift: our compliance group is pushing for 99.95% (monthly) for the inference endpoint used in prod.
- Monthly remedy cadence: we'd like credits to be calculated monthly but with a rolling smoothing (so spikes in one month don't fully tank credits).
- Cap on remedies: procurement prefers a cap at 10% of monthly invoice (we saw higher %s in your standard template).
- Maintenance carveouts: we want a narrower maintenance carveout window and better notification SLAs.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our asks and traffic profile (CloudScale_SLA_Requests.xlsx). Can you share Redwood's best alternative if 99.95% isn't achievable on hosted? Is this something we can solve with Dedicated capacity and a 6‑month commit?

Appreciate a quick read — procurement is trying to lock terms this week.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Ops | CloudScale Inc.
Attachment: CloudScale_SLA_Requests.xlsx (XLSX, 32KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the spreadsheet, that was helpful. A few quick points and a proposed middle ground to keep things moving: 

1) Hosted baseline: our standard hosted SLA is 99.9% monthly for the inference endpoint.
2) Dedicated offering: with Dedicated capacity and a 6‑month minimum commit we can contractually guarantee 99.95% with a smaller credit schedule — that requires capacity reservation and some onboarding / warmup calibration.
3) Hybrid compromise (proposal): 99.92% monthly availability on hosted with a graduated credit ladder and a monthly cap of 8% of the monthly invoice. Credits would be smoothed across a 3‑month rolling window to address your smoothing ask.
4) Maintenance and notifications: we can limit routine maintenance carveouts to a predefined monthly maintenance window and require 48h advance notice for planned windows; emergency maintenance would come with an incident post‑mortem and a shorter notice requirement only for safety/security patches.

I've attached a draft amendment (SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf) that highlights the proposed bands and credit math. Can you confirm whether Procurement would accept 8% cap + 3‑month smoothing as a counter, or whether they need to hold firm at 10%? If they need 99.95, we'll outline Dedicated pricing and commit terms.

Happy to hop on a 30‑minute call today to walk the numbers.

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: Jamie Liao <jamie.l@cloudscale.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.p@cloudscale.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:05:12 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence

Rafael — quick redline from procurement and legal attached. Two main asks from our side after reviewing your proposal: 

- Keep target uptime at 99.95%. CloudScale can agree to a Dedicated commit if the pricing delta is acceptable; please send a ballpark for the 6‑month and 12‑month terms.
- If 99.92 is the only hosted option, Procurement will consider an 8% cap only if the definition of downtime explicitly excludes edge routing incidents (we saw issues at our edge provider last quarter).

We removed the broad maintenance carveout language and tried to tighten the notification obligations. See Redline_SLA_CloudScale.docx for the exact changes.

Jamie
Senior Procurement Manager | CloudScale Inc.
Attachment: Redline_SLA_CloudScale.docx (DOCX, 45KB)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence

Team — forwarding CloudScale's redline (attached). Quick thoughts / negotiation plan: 

- Legal (Kimberly): redline tightens maintenance carveouts and removes edge routing exclusion — do we accept as is for Hosted? If we accept 99.92 on hosted with an 8% cap, we need language that preserves our limited-scope network carveouts (third‑party transit events). Recommend: keep narrow third‑party carveout but require customers to prove correlation (logs/traces) before credit eligibility.

- CS (Marissa): if they demand 99.95 we'll push Dedicated. Can you model the cost delta for 6 vs 12 months and the onboarding lift (warm cache, routing pinning)? Also confirm operational readiness for the tighter notification windows.

Suggested negotiation posture for the call: price Dedicated at ~20% uplift from hosted list for 6‑month and 12% uplift for a 12‑month commit; accept 8% cap with 3‑month smoothing for hosted if we can include a correlation requirement for third‑party network incidents.

If Legal is comfortable, I'll propose the compromise to Jamie/Procurement and include the Dedicated pricing as an alternate.

Thanks,
Rafael

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:41:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence

Rafael / team — reviewed Jamie's redline. Legal notes and recommended edits: 

1) Third‑party carveouts: we can keep a narrow carveout for upstream transit/CDN outages, but require customers to submit correlation evidence (traces, edge provider incident IDs) within 14 days to be eligible for credits. That protects Redwood from broad claims while still being reasonable.
2) Maintenance notices: 48h planned notice is fine; we should preserve the ability to schedule patch windows with shorter notice for critical security issues, but require an incident report and a credit consideration if a planned maintenance exceeds X minutes beyond the window.
3) Cap: 8% monthly cap is acceptable for Hosted only if smoothing is 3 months and if we add a clause that cumulative credits cannot exceed 25% of the invoice over any 12‑month period (protects against long tail claims).

If we agree to the above, we should update SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf and send a mark‑up to CloudScale. CS should confirm the Dedicated pricing assumptions.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir.p@cloudscale.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Jamie Liao <jamie.l@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:02:13 -0500
Subject: Re: SLA amendment: uptime bands & monthly remedy cadence

Rafael / team — thanks for the quick turn. CloudScale can accept the following compromise: 

- Hosted availability: 99.92% monthly, with a monthly credit cap of 8% of the invoice and a 3‑month rolling smoothing window.
- Dedicated alternative: if we sign a 12‑month Reserved Dedicated commitment at the proposed price uplift, Redwood will guarantee 99.95% with a 5% monthly cap. Please send the 12‑month pricing and the onboarding SOW.
- Third‑party carveouts: we accept the correlation evidence requirement.
- Maintenance: 48h notice for planned; emergency security patches allowed with post‑mortem.

We attached a final markup accepting the compromise; please provide a final PDF for signature and a DocuSign link.

Samir
Head of Cloud Ops | CloudScale Inc.
Attachment: SLA_Amendment_Final.pdf (PDF, 92KB); DocuSign: https://docusign.com/xyz123-signature

- Kimberly: finalize final PDF and DocuSign envelope.

Talk Monday if anything changes.

Best,
Rafael
